source.title: Phases of learning dynamics in artificial neural networks: with or without mislabeled data

record.tranche_reason: The study tracks training and test errors across label-noise levels and over training time, bearing on noisy-label fitting and learning order.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original random-label memorization results in its introduction and summary; those citations are not treated as this study's results. It reports its own results for MNIST and says CIFAR10 shows similar results, but gives detailed settings for MNIST only.
record.test_reason: The study trains networks with SGD on randomly corrupted labels and measures training/test errors and learning order, directly testing V2, V4 and V6 with the same basic method and measures as the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' findings: clean samples are learned first, noisy samples are memorized later, and eventual fitting of all training samples accompanies increased test error. Loss separation is greatest in phase II and motivates cleaning. Add their qualification that sufficiently high noise prevents correctly labeled data from driving learning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD and studies training on datasets with randomly mislabeled samples, but analyzes phase dynamics and error trajectories rather than reproducing the original random-label experiment as stated.
record.method_sensitivity: The final test error rises with ρ; the minimum test error increases sharply after a threshold and approaches the final test error when ρ > 0.85.
record.problems: The text gives detailed settings for the MNIST subset but no exact numerical values for the error curves or noise fractions in the prose. CIFAR10 is described only as showing similar results. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: No identifiable completely random-label experiment establishes zero training error, chance test error and unchanged architecture/hyperparameters together.
A small constant-factor training-time comparison between true labels and completely random labels is not established.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
Perfect training fit at every corruption fraction through complete randomization and the chance-level endpoint are not established by the supplied text.
No comparisons involving weight decay, dropout, data augmentation or their removal.

missing.what: The high-noise qualification to clean-first learning: minimum test error approaches final error above ρ = 0.85, and the authors explicitly state that correctly labeled data no longer drives learning.
The authors report similar four-phase learning dynamics on CIFAR10. Record this qualitative cross-dataset result separately, with architecture, noise fractions and numerical outcomes unspecified.
missing.locator: Section 4, paragraph introducing the four learning phases

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Missing numerical detail or untested claim components do not justify limits_scope labels. The supplied figure text does not permit reliable reconstruction of individual plotted values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish the full original claim for a completely random labeling with test error at chance and unchanged settings; the reported experiments vary the fraction of randomly mislabeled samples, and the text does not specify a wholly random-label condition.

Reports how tf changes with noise fraction, but does not quantify a constant-factor training-time comparison against true labels or establish that convergence slows as the corrupted fraction grows in the stated terms.
No shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs are reported.
Does not establish perfect training fit at every noise fraction or a steady test-error rise at each intermediate fraction; detailed numerical values are not stated in the text.
No weight-decay, dropout, or data-augmentation comparison is reported.
Tests the order in which correctly and randomly mislabeled samples are learned, but does not compare a separate fully random-label training run.

rows.subject: fully connected network with two hidden layer (50 hidden units per layer)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with a fraction ρ of randomly mislabeled samples; tracked test error and errors on correctly and incorrectly labeled training samples across four phases.

conditions.value: subset of MNIST data with 400 samples per digit
different values of ρ; exact values not stated in text

rows.measure: Training and test error over training time
rows.value: During phase III (70 − 200 epoch), errors for both correct and incorrect training data decrease to zero; test error increases quickly and reaches a high plateau in phase IV.
rows.note: Detailed phase descriptions are for the MNIST setting. Authors state CIFAR10 shows similar results, without detailed values or settings.
rows.check: Remove V1: a completely random-label condition is not established. Change partial to observed: both training subsets reach zero error, and the phase descriptions explicitly show clean-label learning preceding noisy-label memorization. Missing endpoints do not make the observed effect partial.

rows.subject: fully connected network with two hidden layer (50 hidden units per layer)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the test-error minimum time tm and training-loss minimum time tf across label-noise fractions ρ.

conditions.value: subset of MNIST data with 400 samples per digit
ρ; exact values not stated in text

rows.measure: tm, tf, minimum test error ϵm, and final test error ϵf as functions of ρ
rows.value: tm is almost independent of ρ; tf increases with ρ; ϵf increases with ρ almost linearly; ϵm remains roughly the same when ρ is small, then increases sharply and approaches ϵf when ρ > 0.85.
rows.note: The paper reports qualitative trends in the text, not exact plotted values.
rows.check: The reported increase in tf and almost-linear increase in final test error directly exhibit the tested components. The unquantified constant-factor comparison and chance endpoint are untested, not scope limitations. tf measures the training-loss minimum, not specifically the first attainment of zero training error.

rows.measure: Separation and convergence of per-sample loss distributions
rows.baseline: At time 0, the two distributions are identical.
rows.value: The distributions separate during phase I, reach maximum separation during phase II, close during phase III, and become indistinguishable again near zero loss in phase IV.
rows.note: Supports the reported learning order in this noisy-label setting.
rows.check: The extraction is accurate. Specify that clean-sample losses move downward first while noisy-sample losses initially move slightly upward; separation alone would not establish learning order.
